sources_considered.why: NAACL 2024 study of LLMs on altered versions of familiar tasks. It is directly relevant, but its findings cut both ways, so it is used as context.
PHANTOM RECALL (Oct 2025) documents models reproducing memorized puzzle solutions. It postdates the target period and was not read in full.
Sept 2024 preprint on modified surgeon riddles. It postdates the post and was not read.

receipt.public_excerpt: This suggests that while current LMs may possess abstract task-solving skills to an extent, they often also rely on narrow, non-transferable procedures for task-solving.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows that LLMs rely heavily on familiar patterns when tasks are altered, which fits Marcus's picture. The same paper finds some abstract task-solving ability, which cuts against 'literally don't reason'. Whether either finding counts as 'reasoning' depends on a definition.

unresolved_gaps: There is no agreed operational definition of 'reasoning' against which to test 'literally don't'.
No independent record of the exact ChatGPT output on Fraser's riddle was found. The mechanism behind it cannot be observed from outside.
